questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Take the wheels.

options.text: Let the wheels be taken by you.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Let the wheels be taken by you.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• To convert an active sentence to passive, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence, and the verb is changed to a passive form (usually "be" + past participle).
 
• **In this case, "wheels" is the object of the active sentence "Take the wheels." Therefore, it becomes the subject of the passive sentence.**
 
• **"Be taken" is the passive form of "take."**
 
• "By you" is added to indicate who is doing the action (in this case, taking the wheels).
 
• Thus, the given sentence in passive form will be:
 
 
• Let the wheels be taken by you.
 
 

Hence, **the correct answer is option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1, "Let the wheels take you," is in active voice and does not match the given sentence in passive voice.
 
• Option 2, "Let you take the wheels," is in active voice and has the subject and object reversed from the original sentence.
 
• Option 4, "Let wheels you take," is not grammatically correct.

questions.question:

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

If things were not going to be normal / after the pandemic, mankind will / have to accept the New Normal.

options.text: have to accept the New Normal
If things were not going to be normal

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**If things were not going to be normal.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **In the given sentence, the error lies in the part," If things were not going to be normal."**
 
• **The verb tense in this part of the sentence is incorrect. **
 
• **"Were" is in the past tense, while "will" is in the future tense.**
 
• The sentence is referring to a situation in future. 
 
• Thus, to maintain proper tense agreement, the correct version of this sentence would be:
 
 
• "If things are not going to be normal after the pandemic, mankind will have to accept the New Normal."
 
 

Thus, **the correct answer is option 3**.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Let me buy an expensive bag for my friend.

options.text: I request you to buy an expensive bag for my friend.
An excessive bag will be bought by me for my friend.
Let an expensive bag was bought by me for my friend.
Let an expensive bag be bought by me for my friend.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Let an expensive bag be bought by me for my friend.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in active form i.e. the action performed by the subject is expressed by the verb.
 
 
• Example: She(subject) wrote(verb) a letter(object).
 
 
 
• In passive voice, the the subject is acted upon by the verb or action in the sentence.
 
 
• The structure of sentence in passive voice is: Object+ verb+ subject.
 
 
 
• **The sentence is in active voice with the subject "Let me" performing the action of buying.**
 
• **To convert it into passive voice, we need to make the object "an expensive bag" the subject and use the passive form of the verb "buy" (be + past participle).**
 
• The sentence in passive voice will have the structure: "Let an expensive bag be bought by me for my friend."

Hence, **the correct answer is option 4**.

questions.question:

Arthur has some strange ideas, but on this occasion, I am __inclined__ to agree with him.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**tended.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let us understand the meaning of the given and the marked words:
 
 
• **"Inclined" means wanting to behave in a particular way**.

 
 
• Example: If you are so inclined, you can watch TV.
 
 
 
• **"Tended" means to have a tendency or inclination towards something**, which fits the context of the sentence.
 
 
• ​Example: She tended to monopolize the conversation.
 
 
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, "inclined to agree" means that the speaker is leaning towards agreeing with Arthur.
 
• Thus, the word "tended" is the synonym of the word "inclined."

Hence, **the correct answer is option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.**

__While he saw the bear__, he ran to the nearest tree, dropped his gun and climbed to a safe place.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **When he saw the bear**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence can be improved by replacing "**While**" with "**When**."
 
• "**While**" typically indicates a simultaneous occurrence or action, often without implying a direct cause-and-effect relationship.
 
 
• **For example-** *While I was cooking dinner, my friend arrived at my house.*
 
 
 
• "**When**" is used to indicate a specific point in time or a particular event that triggers another action. It implies a cause-and-effect relationship.
 
 
• **For example-** *When I heard the thunder, I decided to stay indoors.*
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, "**When**" is a more suitable choice because it establishes that the sighting of the bear prompted the person to take immediate action.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

**Improved sentence**: *When he saw the bear, he ran to the nearest tree, dropped his gun and climbed to a safe place.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**No sooner did he see**" is not appropriate as it changes the meaning of the sentence and implies that he ran to the tree immediately upon seeing the bear.
 
• "**Hardly he saw the bear**" is grammatically incorrect as it should be "Hardly had he seen the bear" to be in the correct past tense.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate **antonym **of the word given in the bracket to fill in the blank.

There are ______ (definite) weaknesses in their security arrangements.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Vague**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Definite **refers to something that is unmistakable, well-defined, and leaves no room for doubt or interpretation. (किसी ऐसी चीज़ को संदर्भित करता है जो असंदिग्ध, अच्छी तरह से परिभाषित है, और संदेह या व्याख्या के लिए कोई जगह नहीं छोड़ती है)

 
 
• **For example- ***The scientist presented definite evidence supporting her theory, leaving no room for scepticism.*
 
 
 
• Marked option **Vague **is used to describe situations where there is a lack of clarity, precision, or specificity, which can lead to confusion or uncertainty. (स्पष्टता, सटीकता या विशिष्टता की कमी, जिससे भ्रम या अनिश्चितता पैदा हो सकती है)
 
 
• **For example- ***The directions he gave were so vague that I couldn't figure out which way to turn.*
 
 
 
• From here, it is clear that the **antonym **of 'definite' is 'vague'.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

This will be most difficult of /the adjustments we have to make / because we have been used to spending a lot on guests.

options.text: the adjustments we have to make
This will be most difficult of
because we have been used to

questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: **This will be most difficult of**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error is in the omission of the article "**the**" before "**most difficult**."
 
• In English, articles (definite and indefinite) play a crucial role in indicating whether we are talking about specific or general things.
 
• In this case, using "**the**" before "**most difficult**" helps to specify that particular adjustment among others.
 
• The phrase "**the most difficult of**" indicates a comparison among a group of adjustments, stating that one particular adjustment is the most challenging.
 
• The article "**the**" is necessary before "most difficult" to make the comparison clear and grammatically correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is** option 3** which contains the error.

**Corrected sentence:** *This will be the most difficult of the adjustments we have to make because we have been used to spending a lot on guests.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

The family __has visit__ many parts of Europe when the man was working with an international educational agency.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **had visited**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in the past tense, indicating that the family's visits to Europe happened before the man stopped working with the international educational agency.
 
• "**Had visited**" is the **past perfect tense**, which is used to describe an action that happened before another action in the past.
 
 
• **Form**: *Subject + "had" + past participle (v3 form of the verb).*
 
• **For example-** *After he had finished his work, he went for a walk.*
 
 
 
• In this case, the family's visits to Europe happened before the man stopped working with the agency.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

**Corrected sentence**: *The family had visited many parts of Europe when the man was working with an international educational agency.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**are visited**" is in the present tense and does not match the past tense of the sentence.
 
• "**have visit**" is the present perfect tense, which is also incorrect.
 
• "**has visiting**" is a present continuous tense, which is not appropriate for past action.
